clue.text: R. Hood wrests with foe possibly in his habitat

indicators.note: possibly says the letters of R. Hood, wrests and foe could be arranged another way

explanation.surface: Robin Hood grapples with an enemy somewhere out in his familiar woodland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' tells you to rearrange R HOOD + WRESTS + FOE; 'with' is only a link. The definition leans on the R. Hood in the clue: his habitat is the Nottinghamshire forest of the legend.
explanation.definitionFit: The outlaw of English legend lived with his band in this Nottinghamshire woodland.

clue.text: Lost clot, camper going astray, one pursuing hobby

indicators.note: going astray says the letters of lost, clot and camper wander out of order

explanation.surface: A lost idiot camper wandering off course is busy with some pastime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going astray' rearranges LOST + CLOT + CAMPER.
explanation.definitionFit: A philatelist is a person whose pastime is gathering postage issues.

clue.text: Material used to make the last icon

indicators.note: used to make says a run of letters within the words the last icon forms the answer

explanation.surface: A fabric went into creating the final religious image.
explanation.walkthrough: 'used to make' signals a run inside 'thE LAST ICon'.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a stretchy fabric or cord used in clothing.

clue.text: Outside game naughty fellow gives non-PC signal

indicators.note: Outside says the jumbled fellow goes around the name of a game
naughty says the letters of fellow misbehave and change order

parts.note: whist is a card game

explanation.surface: A misbehaving man in the open air makes an offensive gesture during a match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Outside' looks like a place for the game, but it puts the rearranged 'fellow' (from 'naughty') round the card game. 'gives' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A two-note sound aimed at a passing woman is now seen as sexist, hence not politically correct.

clue.text: Strangeness a couple won't show

explanation.surface: Oddly enough, a pair of guests fails to turn up.
explanation.walkthrough: The second sense is cryptic: an odd thing, like a lone sock, is one whose partner is missing, so the couple is not on show.
explanation.definitionFit: Peculiarity is weirdness, and an unmatched single item is something whose pair cannot be seen.

clue.text: Wanting to have lock for stronghold

parts.note: to be for something is to be in favour of it or want it
a tress is a lock of hair

explanation.surface: Someone after a lock wants it for a secure castle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lock' is a lock of hair, not something on a door.
explanation.definitionFit: A castle or fortified place is a defensive stronghold.

clue.text: Rubbish in brother's collection

indicators.note: in says the answer sits inside the word brother's

explanation.surface: There's junk among the items a brother has collected.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters sit inside bROTher's.
explanation.definitionFit: Rot is nonsense, as in 'talking rubbish'.

clue.text: Attitudes accepted by most ancestors

indicators.note: accepted by says the answer is held within the words most ancestors

explanation.surface: Positions taken were endorsed by the majority of our forebears.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across mosT ANCEStors.
explanation.definitionFit: Stances are positions or points of view on an issue.

clue.text: See dignitaries

parts.note: a see is a bishop's diocese, and the dignitaries are the cathedral's governing body of senior clergy

explanation.definitionFit: The senior priest and canons who run a cathedral form its governing body.

clue.text: Girl I took in hand benefited

parts.note: Ava is a girl's name
taken as written
to take someone in hand can mean to guide them, so led

explanation.surface: A girl I had under my charge did well out of it.
explanation.definitionFit: To have availed oneself of something is to have profited or gained from it.

clue.text: Some camera traced the hectic daily round

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A security camera has tracked commuters on their frantic everyday grind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Some' signals that part of the words 'camera traced' gives the answer: cameRA TRACEd.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is the usual idiom for the exhausting competitive routine of working life.

clue.text: Place ram goes around

indicators.note: goes around turns the word for ram so it is read backwards

parts.note: a tup is a ram, a male sheep

explanation.surface: A ram trots in circles around a spot in the field.
explanation.walkthrough: TUP is a dialect word for a ram, common in crosswords; 'goes around' turns it to give PUT.
explanation.definitionFit: To place something somewhere is to set or position it there.

clue.text: Rose may be attached to this in garden

definitions.text: Rose may be attached to this in garden

parts.words: Rose may be attached to this in garden
parts.note: a rose here is not the flower but the perforated nozzle that sprinkles water, fitted to a gardener's spout

explanation.definitionFit: A gardener's vessel with a long spout often carries a sprinkler head called a rose.

clue.text: One topless bather, terrible one likely to cause offence

indicators.note: terrible says the remaining letters, with bather and one, are thrown into disorder
topless says the first letter of One is taken off

explanation.surface: A topless bather on the beach is shocking enough to give offence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'topless' removes the O from One to leave NE; 'terrible' then rearranges NE + BATHER + ONE.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes a remark or joke that is risque or uncomfortably close to the truth.

clue.text: Plant that's yellow and more or less concealed

parts.note: or is the heraldic term for gold or yellow
c, short for circa, means about or more or less
hid means concealed

explanation.surface: A plant with yellow blooms that is half hidden in the undergrowth.
explanation.walkthrough: OR is heraldry's gold, C stands for circa ('about'), and HID is concealed; 'and' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a family of flowering plants prized for their exotic blooms.

clue.text: Fool with a second moral offence, a murderer

parts.note: an ass is a fool
taken as written
a sin is a moral offence

explanation.surface: A foolish man commits a second wrong and turns out to be a killer.
explanation.definitionFit: This kind of killer murders a prominent person, usually for political ends.

clue.text: Walter is hard — it's his language!

parts.note: Sir Walter Scott was the ... novelist
taken as written
h is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: The novelist Walter is tough going, being written in his native tongue.
explanation.walkthrough: Sir Walter Scott was a Scottish novelist, so 'his language' points back to him.
explanation.definitionFit: Scott was born in Edinburgh, and his novels use the speech of his homeland.

clue.text: War paint in smear across one quiet street

indicators.note: across means the word for smear stretches over the other pieces, holding them inside

parts.note: to lick paint on is to smear it on
I is the Roman numeral one
p, piano, is the musical direction for quiet

explanation.surface: A rioter's face paint is smeared across one quiet back street.
explanation.walkthrough: 'War paint' is a jocular name for women's make-up, not face paint for battle; 'across' has the smear word wrapping the other pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: War paint is a humorous term for cosmetics, and this is the coloured stick worn on the mouth.

clue.text: Bag woman occupies seaside building

indicators.note: occupies says the woman's name sits inside the building

parts.note: a pier is a structure built out over the sea at a resort
Ann is a woman's name

explanation.surface: A woman sets up shop in a building on the seafront with her bag.
explanation.walkthrough: Seaside piers, long walkways over the sea with amusements and shops, are a fixture of British resorts; 'occupies' puts the woman inside one.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a bag or basket slung over a bicycle or a pack animal.

clue.text: Good person a short time in charge, not dynamic

parts.note: St, a saint, is a good person
taken as written
t is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A good person who holds office only briefly never achieves any momentum.
explanation.definitionFit: Something stationary and unchanging is the opposite of dynamic.

clue.text: Get the wind up!

parts.note: to get the wind up usually means to become scared, but read literally it describes air carried upward

explanation.definitionFit: A rising current of warm air lifts gliders and birds skyward.

clue.text: Young hooligan, I am upsetting girl

indicators.note: upsetting, in a down clue, turns the hooligan and I am upside down so they read backwards

parts.note: ned is Scottish slang for a young hooligan
taken as written, I and am

explanation.surface: A young thug says he is upsetting a girl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upsetting' reverses the whole of NED + IAM. NED is Scottish slang for a young troublemaker.
explanation.definitionFit: A maiden is a young unmarried woman in older usage.

clue.text: Strong fruit juice getting one to focus attention?

explanation.surface: Squash in the glass helps a worker keep their mind on the job.
explanation.walkthrough: The first sense is the undiluted juice you water down; the second is the verb meaning to fix the mind. 'getting one to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Juice reduced to a strong syrup is called this as a noun, and as a verb it means to fix one's mind on something.

clue.text: Woman in tree-lined road looking back

indicators.note: looking back says the abbreviation for the road is read in reverse

parts.note: Ave, avenue, is a road often lined with trees

explanation.surface: A woman on a leafy avenue glances over her shoulder.
explanation.definitionFit: Eva is a woman's first name.

clue.text: Old equipment used by foreign friend for art

parts.note: a rig is a set of equipment
ami is French for friend

explanation.surface: A French friend makes art from some old gear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'used by' is a link joining the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the Japanese craft of folding paper into decorative shapes.

clue.text: Bristle, top bit taken off grass

indicators.note: top bit taken off, in a down clue, removes the first letter of the word for grass

parts.note: a lawn is an area of grass

explanation.surface: The tip of a blade of grass has been snipped off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'top bit taken off' removes the first letter from LAWN.
explanation.definitionFit: An awn is the stiff hair-like spike on the head of barley and other cereals.

clue.text: Mug excited by silly motor ad

indicators.note: silly says the letters of motor and ad are jumbled into a new order

explanation.surface: Only a sucker would be thrilled by a daft car advert.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mug' is British slang for a gullible person, not a cup or a face. 'silly' rearranges MOTOR + AD.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are informal words for someone easily used and taken advantage of.

clue.text: Bismarck, one man with opportunity to get going in revolution

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
Ron is a man's name
a chance is an opportunity

indicators.note: in revolution says the word for get going is turned round and read backwards

parts.note: to roll is to start moving, as in let's roll

explanation.surface: A Prussian statesman seizes his chance to start a revolution.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in revolution' reverses ROLL to LLOR; 'with' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Otto von Bismarck, the Prussian statesman who unified Germany, was nicknamed this for his iron will.
